# Offline layout engines — Windows desktop candidate

All computation is local, triggered only by explicit Auto Layout. Inputs: bounded IDs, node dimensions, edges, group membership, viewport. No note bodies/attachments, network access or business JSON reads/writes.

The existing grouped option continues to use the embedded ELK Worker. Other options require Node18+ on PATH (restart Obsidian after installing/changing PATH). CP-SAT additionally requires the Windows `py` launcher and Python3.12 x64. Its pinned OR-Tools/dependencies are included under python-deps; nothing is pip-installed into a global environment. ABI: cp312-cp312-win_amd64. The package is approximately168MiB. Other platforms/mobile are not certified; missing capabilities fail without modifying the graph.

CP-SAT solver budget5s; Python startup+solve budget15s; overall child budget20s. Cancel/timeout terminates only the authored process tree. Rectangular CP-SAT chooses both occupied grid spans freely up to the node count, with abs(columns-rows)<=3 (including internal empty bands), no fixed four-column cap and no transpose. Physical envelope/viewport extent (precision 1e-4), aspect error (1e-4) and area rank ahead of physical edge length using a proven dominant integer weight. OPTIMAL proves only this discrete objective; FEASIBLE is a bounded-time incumbent. Routing is separate and may enlarge the envelope or reject the result. Moving group repair is bypassed for this option; only grid-preserving translation/spacing expansion is allowed. Solver diagnostics retain spans/status/objective/bound. Concave CP-SAT retains its independent existing model and eight-column bound. Other engines retain bounded group repair. No infeasibility claim extends beyond the model. Misframing, node/route collisions and existing route separation failures cannot be applied. Native ELK changes to libavoid routing when group repair moves nodes, and the preview labels this.

Offline dependencies retain package source, metadata and licenses:

- elkjs0.12.0 — EPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0-or-later; node_modules/elkjs/LICENSE.md; upstream https://github.com/kieler/elkjs
- webcola3.4.0 — MIT; node_modules/webcola/LICENSE; upstream https://github.com/tgdwyer/WebCola
- libavoid-js0.5.0-beta.5 — LGPL-2.1-or-later; node_modules/libavoid-js/LICENSE; independently replaceable JS/WASM files under dist, upstream source https://github.com/Aksem/libavoid-js . No obfuscation/relink restriction is added by this adapter.
- OR-Tools9.15.6755 — Apache-2.0; python-deps/ortools-9.15.6755.dist-info/LICENSE; upstream https://github.com/google/or-tools . Transitive Python and d3 licenses remain alongside installed packages. Full distribution file hashes: ../picker-manifest.json in staging release (outside plugin folder).

This package is a staging candidate, not a deployment assertion. Do not copy data.json, cache, indexes or settings when deploying code. Initial installation requires the complete offline dependency package. The 2026-09-21 refinement is a five-file update only: main.js, styles.css, layout-engines/engine.cjs, layout-engines/placement.py and this README. Do not copy staging dependency junctions or replace unchanged dependencies/concave modules. Runtime deployment requires final verification and confirmation.

## Weighted constraint grid candidate — 2026-09-22

The new `cpsat-weighted` option (加权约束网格 · 重点连线) prioritizes fewer crossings and less detouring on important connections, with a smaller endpoint-proximity preference. Existing six options retain their behavior. This remains a bounded heuristic; it does not prove global optimality or guarantee a crossing reduction on every graph.

The Hub owns optional integer `stateGraph.edges[].weightScore` in 0..99, independently per directed edge. Missing means 50 without backfill; 0 retains the edge. Invalid present values are rejected. Versions 1 and 2 remain supported. Direction scores persist through the existing identity/CAS, queue, fresh-disk, save/readback and audit path. Editing a score does not move nodes or reroute: select the new algorithm and explicitly preview/apply. Reciprocal directions keep separate scores, IDs and comments, but their shared visual path takes the larger strength. This cannot prioritize one direction's geometry independently from the other on that shared path.

Strength is `1 + 3 * sqrt(score / 99)`; visual-path strengths are then divided by their mean. The ratio between any two path weights is at most 4:1. Score 99 versus default 50 is about 1.28:1, deliberately compressing the high range; score is a preference, not a probability or observed frequency. Empty-edge graphs have no normalization division.

For all candidates in one request, fixed length scale `L = max(100, maximum node width)`. The complete objective, divided by `max(1, number of visual paths)`, is:

`6 * weighted(crossings + touches) + 2 * weighted(excess route length) / L + 0.4 * weighted(near-parallel exposure) / L + 0.15 * weighted(bends) + 0.05 * weighted(endpoint distance) / L`.

Contact pairs use the mean of their two weights and are deduplicated by path pair and intersection point. Ordinary touches receive the same penalty as crossings, preventing a crossing from escaping the objective by landing on an elbow. Excess length is route Manhattan length minus endpoint Manhattan distance, floored at zero. Near-parallel exposure accumulates projected overlap for lane gaps below 16px, attenuated by `1-gap/16`. The hard checks still reject shared positive-length segments and protected approach/port violations. Weighted improvement can trade more low-priority bends, length or crossings for clearer high-priority paths; raw and weighted diagnostics are retained for inspection.

The standard rectangular CP-SAT engine supplies a fully checked baseline. Current saved geometry is an additional seed only if its dimensions, uniform grid, group frames and complete routes pass all current hard checks. Search proposes legal node swaps and moves to empty cells, combining weighted crossing/detour hotspots and weighted proximity when shortlisting. Each trial routes with protected routing first, then libavoid if needed, and must pass the complete geometry checks. A candidate must retain at least 95% of the reference fit. The best completed feasible candidate is retained, including the baseline; there is no partially scored acceptance.

Before moving nodes, one seed-reroute proposal retains the chosen baseline positions and inserts paths in descending weight order, under the same trial and time caps. Router insertion order is only a proposal mechanism, not a mathematical priority guarantee; complete weighted quality decides acceptance. The original baseline and its diagnostics remain intact if this proposal is invalid, worse or times out.

Limits: 1–60 nodes, at most 180 visual paths, 30 nonempty groups and 1200 scored route segments. Baseline plus search share a 17s coordinator deadline inside the existing 20s parent cap; baseline child at most 9s, routing child at most 2s/remaining budget. At most 12 routing trials, two local rounds, and 2048 placement checks/600ms per round. Startup or difficult feasibility can exhaust the budget; failure preserves the graph. Actual Windows timeout and cancellation terminate only the authored Node/Python process tree. There are no new dependencies or network calls.

Both Preview and Apply independently validate uniform-grid metadata, node dimensions/identities, occupied spans with `abs(columns-rows)<=3`, complete paths and existing group/port protections. Preview, Cancel, score edits and helper computations never save geometry. Apply uses the existing transaction and exact revision-bound Undo. A graph mutation in any host invalidates pending geometry; diagnostics and grid certificates are transient and do not migrate saved layout schemas.

This candidate's deployment list is exactly five files: `main.js`, `layout-engines/engine.cjs`, `layout-engines/weighted.cjs`, `layout-engines/weighted-job.cjs`, and `layout-engines/README.md`. The last two JavaScript modules are new. All dependencies, styles, manifests and old engine modules remain unchanged. Do not copy test files, geometry fixtures, dependency junctions or owner data. Staging browser tests use a mocked Obsidian host and real offline helpers; they do not assert native Obsidian acceptance. Deploy only after final review and user confirmation, with fresh target-hash checks and byte backups.
